title: Rochdale Council Faces £15 Million Budget Deficit by 2029
excerpt: Rochdale Council is projected to face a £15 million budget deficit by 2029 if no action is taken, according to the latest financial forecast presented to town hall officials.
content_html:
Rochdale Council is facing a projected budget deficit of £15.227 million by the financial year 2029/30 if no measures are implemented. The latest budget forecast, presented to town hall officials, highlights that this shortfall is anticipated due to rising wage costs, inflation, and increased pressures in adult social care and children’s services.

The finance team has expressed uncertainty regarding the annual government funding settlement, which complicates future budget planning. Budget documents indicate a risk that the finance settlement for 2029/30 may not include a continuation of the Recovery Grant, which is currently confirmed only until 2028/29 and amounts to approximately £15 million.

In adult social care, the 'real living wage' is increasing at a rate higher than anticipated, further straining financial resources. An additional allocation of £1.5 million per year has been incorporated into future cost estimates. Overspending in children’s services has also exceeded initial forecasts, a trend that has been noted in recent years, according to the meeting held on July 28.

Councillor Daniel Meredith remarked on the ongoing efforts to establish new care homes and children’s homes, stating that significant work is being done to address the challenges in these services. The council has made savings of £204.5 million from its revenue budget since 2010/11, but the projected gaps indicate that savings of £6 million will be necessary by 2028/29, escalating to £15 million by 2029/30.

title: Rochdale's Local Plan for Future Development Moves Forward
excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan, outlining development strategies until 2039, is set for public consultation after council approval. It includes plans for new housing and transport hubs.
content_html:
A plan that will shape Rochdale’s future over the next 13 years has moved closer to implementation following approval from council leaders. The Rochdale Local Plan outlines how the borough will develop until 2039, including the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes to local transport hubs.

The council has refined a 175-page document, which will now enter a public consultation phase. The formal adoption of the plan is anticipated later in 2027. Initially, the plan required that 20 per cent of new housing developments be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this adjustment does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, noting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding the previous target.

Housing is a central focus of the plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone initiative. This strategy, adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils, aims to construct around 175,000 homes across the region over the next two decades. The Local Plan is expected to attract investment and facilitate major redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is a key component of the plan, aiming to transform areas around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This strategy includes enhancements to stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a proposed new station at Slattocks. The plan also incorporates improved walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to boost the local economy and enhance the quality of life for residents.

title: Severely Neglected Toddler Rushed to Hospital After Social Services Case Closed
excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
content_html:
A 19-month-old girl, referred to as Child K1, was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a recent Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The review reported that the toddler was found to be severely emaciated, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age, and covered in sores.

The review detailed that the child was severely dehydrated and had no fatty tissue on her body when she was admitted to critical care in February 2025. Medical professionals noted that she displayed "paper-thin skin" and had open pressure sores extending along her back, hips, and bottom. The case was closed despite warnings about a mother's neglect, who was only 17 when the child was born.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the toddler's mother had struggled with mental health issues and had avoided contact with social workers and health visitors. Following an anonymous tip in December 2024, social workers visited the home and confirmed the child's poor condition but were unable to secure consent for further intervention from the mother, leading to the case being closed due to insufficient evidence of significant harm.

Nineteen days after the case closure, the child was admitted to hospital, where medical staff noted a range of complications that could have led to death if not treated promptly. The findings of the review have prompted Rochdale Borough's Safeguarding Children Partnership to accept the conclusions and take action to address the issues identified.

title: Baby Found in Critical Condition After Social Services Closed Case
excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was rushed to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, revealing severe neglect and malnutrition.
content_html:
A 19-month-old girl was admitted to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale. The toddler, referred to as Child K1, was found to be severely malnourished, weighing just 9.7lb (4.4kg), less than half the expected weight for her age.

The review revealed that the child was covered in sores and had no fatty tissue on her body. Medical staff noted her skin was "paper-thin" and that she displayed signs of severe dehydration. The case was closed despite concerns raised about a mother’s ability to care for her, as she had reportedly avoided contact with social workers and health visitors for weeks.

The review, conducted by expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall, highlighted that the child's grandmother had taken her to the hospital after she refused to eat. During this visit, family members informed hospital staff that the child was being neglected. Following this, the case was referred to Rochdale's Children's Social Care team, which initially assessed the mother as willing to accept support.

However, after an anonymous tip-off in December 2024 alleging severe neglect, social workers visited the home but were unable to secure the mother's consent for further intervention. A multi-agency strategy meeting concluded that the threshold for further action had not been met, leading to the case being closed. Nineteen days later, the child was admitted to critical care, suffering from multiple complications that could have been life-threatening without timely medical intervention.

title: Fire Breaks Out in Smallbridge, Rochdale
excerpt: A fire broke out in Smallbridge, Rochdale, on Friday evening, prompting a response from firefighters who worked through the night to extinguish the flames and monitor the aftermath.
content_html:
A fire broke out in an open area on Spring Mill Walk in Smallbridge at around 8:15pm on Friday, July 24. Aerial images captured the impact of the fire, which burned overnight and produced large plumes of black smoke visible across Rochdale.

Firefighters worked throughout the night to extinguish the flames and remained on the scene until around 1pm on Saturday, damping down hotspots and monitoring the aftermath. Dramatic photos on social media showed the extent of the fire, which involved a large quantity of waste at the site.

Officials from the Environment Agency were called in, and the local council was alerted due to the nature of the incident. Pictures taken by a drone camera later revealed a significant area of scorched earth and debris left behind by the fire.

No injuries have been reported as a result of the fire. Fire crews are expected to continue monitoring the site in the coming days.
